sub_units.name: Performance Optimization
sub_units.content: Performance optimization in React involves measuring and improving the rendering speed of your application. Key strategies include using tools like React DevTools Profiler, avoiding anonymous functions in render, and optimizing list rendering.

sub_units.name: React.memo
sub_units.content: React.memo is a higher-order component for functional components. If your component renders the same result given the same props, you can wrap it in React.memo to skip re-rendering the component and reuse the last rendered result.

sub_units.name: Lazy Loading & Suspense
sub_units.content: React.lazy lets you define a component that is loaded dynamically. This helps reduce the bundle size and load components on demand. Suspense allows you to show a placeholder (like a spinner) while the lazy component is loading.

sub_units.name: Code Splitting
sub_units.content: Code splitting is a feature supported by bundlers like Webpack and Vite. It allows you to split your code into various bundles which can then be loaded on demand or in parallel, significantly improving the initial load time of your application.

sub_units.name: Error Boundaries
sub_units.content: Error boundaries are React components that catch JavaScript errors anywhere in their child component tree, log those errors, and display a fallback UI instead of the component tree that crashed. They catch errors during rendering and in lifecycle methods.

sub_units.name: HOC
sub_units.content: A higher-order component (HOC) is an advanced technique in React for reusing component logic. HOCs are not part of the React API, per se. They are a pattern that emerges from React's compositional nature. A HOC is a function that takes a component and returns a new component.

sub_units.name: React Patterns
sub_units.content: React patterns like Render Props and Compound Components provide structured ways to share stateful logic or build complex components that are easy to use and customize. Mastering these patterns leads to more maintainable and flexible codebases.
